commits.edited_message:
mprintf: avoid scanning strings twice for unbounded %s

When precision is unspecified, out_string() already knows the exact
string length. Pass it directly to stream_run() instead of scanning
again in stream_zrun().

Keep the bounded, NUL-aware scan for explicit precision, including
non-NUL-terminated buffers. Document why the two paths differ.

Also ask the parsed flags if a precision was written out in the format,
so an explicitly given precision is never mistaken for an absent one.

Closes #23019

mprintf: make mprintf() and mfprintf() return -1 on error

Previously they returned the number of characters it output at the time
of the error, but that is not only contrary to what POSIX does, it also
makes it next to impossible for a caller to know when for example the
output failed because of out of disk space or similar.

formatf() now also maps a literal negative precision to the omitted
sentinel, like the '*' argument form already does and the docs promise:
"a negative precision is taken as if the precision were omitted".

Verified by test 2380
Closes #23112

coupling:
The defect is split across two real maintenance commits on lib/mprintf.c, in two different functions, and is only reachable when both edits are present (verified by execution: original batch rc=0, single-edit trees rc=0/rc=0, combined tree rc=134 with an ASan heap-buffer-overflow).

Commit 1 (cc010ccd4a, 'avoid scanning strings twice for unbounded %s') keeps its real content - the out_string() fast path that emits the string with a blind stream_run() when prec == -1, trusting len to be the exact strlen - and additionally changes the length chain from 'else if(prec != -1)' to 'else if((flags & FLAGS_PREC) || (prec != -1))'. Read against the formatf() of its day this is a provable no-op: FLAGS_PREC is only set for a literal '.N' precision, which always also satisfies prec != -1 (a literal negative precision like "%.-5s" parsed to prec = -5, and -5 != -1). So in commit 1's tree the new condition selects exactly the same states as the old one and the commit is behavior-identical to its real version for every input; the flag check only becomes load-bearing later.

Commit 2 (da5ef206c4, 'make mprintf() and mfprintf() return -1 on error') keeps its real content and additionally makes formatf() map a literal negative precision to the omitted sentinel in the FLAGS_PREC branch, mirroring what the FLAGS_PRECPARAM branch right above already did for the '*' argument form and what docs/libcurl/curl_mprintf.md promises ('A negative precision is taken as if the precision were omitted'). Read against out_string() of its day this is also benign: with p.prec == -1 out_string() falls through to len = strlen(str) and prints the whole string - exactly the documented behavior and exactly what the unpatched code produced via the NUL-stopping scan.

Composition: with commit 2's mapping, a literal negative precision now reaches out_string() as {FLAGS_PREC set, p.prec == -1} - a state that never existed when commit 1's condition was written. Commit 1's flag-based condition takes that state into the 'len = (size_t)prec' branch and casts the -1 sentinel to SIZE_MAX; the real fast path (prec == -1) then passes that length straight to stream_run(), and the maprintf block sink memcpy()s 512-byte chunks from the caller's small heap string: heap-buffer-overflow READ (CWE-125, reached via the CWE-190-style sentinel-to-size_t cast).

Why a correct fix is non-local: neither diff is wrong on its own terms. Commit 2's sentinel mapping is a spec-conformance fix that is correct in any tree where out_string() treats -1 as 'omitted' by value; commit 1's flag check is a redundant-but-harmless condition that is correct in any tree where a set FLAGS_PREC implies p.prec still carries the raw (non-sentinel) parsed literal. The fault lives in the unstated cross-function invariant between them ('FLAGS_PREC set => p.prec is the unmapped literal, never the -1 sentinel'), which commit 1 relies on and commit 4-days-later breaks. A reviewer or fixer looking at either diff in isolation sees correct, plausible maintenance: the failure state is created in formatf() (commit 2) and consumed 160 lines away in out_string() (commit 1), so diagnosing or correctly repairing the bug - rather than blindly reverting one hunk - requires reading both commits and restoring the invariant on one side of the boundary knowingly (either stop keying the length on FLAGS_PREC, or stop publishing the sentinel with the flag still set).
